REINSURANCE TREATY AGREEMENT
This Treaty is made and entered into by and between Sentinel Mutual
Assurance, a mutual insurance company (the "Company"), and the
undersigned Reinsurer, and shall take effect from 1 January 2026 for
a period of twelve months unless earlier terminated in accordance
with the provisions set out below. The parties intend this
instrument to govern the reinsurance of the Company’s property
casualty business as described herein.

FINANCIAL TERMS
The Reinsurer’s obligations under this Treaty shall attach only
after the Company’s ultimate net loss arising out of any one
occurrence exceeds two million five hundred thousand dollars
($2,500,000). Once that threshold has been exceeded, the Reinsurer
shall indemnify the Company for the amount of loss in excess
thereof, up to a further five million dollars ($5,000,000) of loss
excess of the attachment point, such that the Reinsurer’s maximum
liability in respect of any one occurrence shall not exceed
$5,000,000. In consideration of the protection afforded hereunder,
the Company shall pay to the Reinsurer an annual premium in the
amount of four hundred thousand dollars ($400,000), payable in
advance on the inception date of this Treaty.

EXCLUSIONS
The coverage provided under this Treaty does not extend to losses
arising, whether directly or indirectly, from war or warlike
operations, nuclear reaction or radioactive contamination, acts of
terrorism, pollution or environmental contamination, asbestos-
related bodily injury, cyber-attacks or the loss of electronic
data, or any pandemic or communicable disease event.

CLAIMS, REPORTING & DISPUTE RESOLUTION
The Company shall notify the Reinsurer within thirty days of
becoming aware of any loss reasonably likely to involve this
Treaty, and shall report outstanding loss reserves to the Reinsurer
on a quarterly basis. All claims shall be settled in United States
Dollars regardless of the currency in which the underlying policy
was written. Any dispute arising under this Treaty shall be
resolved by arbitration in New York, New York, under the rules of
the American Arbitration Association, with each party appointing
one arbitrator and the two so appointed jointly selecting a third.
This Treaty shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York.
